body.statement: Can the handle in \(\mathrm{def:multiplier\text{-}interval\text{-}handle}\) be turned into a computable interval \(\mathcal I_n(\alpha)\) satisfying \[\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{\mathbf P\in\mathcal P^{\mathrm{reg}}}\mathbb P_n\{\tau_n\in\mathcal I_n(\alpha)\}\ge1-\alpha,\] uniformly across fixed, vanishing, and exact gaps on the scaled local-risk axis, having root-\(n\) excess length controlled above and below by the \(d_n\)-diameter of its localized near-minimizer set and worst-case upper envelope \(\omega^{\star}\), and becoming first-order equivalent to the ordinary Wald interval for \(k_n^{\star}\) along every \(\mathbf P\in\mathcal P^{\mathrm{global,reg}}\) with \(\min_{l\ne k_n^{\star}}\{\mathfrak r_{n,l}-\mathfrak r_{n,k_n^{\star}}\}\ge\varepsilon\) and \(b_{n,k_n^{\star}}=o(n^{-1/2})\)?
body.justification: Uniform coverage and oracle adaptation must be proved together; otherwise a projection interval can be valid but useless or a localized interval can silently fail at a tie.
body.gap: Patel, DiTraglia, Zuber, and Burgess allow a user-chosen worst-case coverage loss for a fixed focused-instrument problem, while Zrnic and Fithian localize generic target sets; neither gives full nominal coverage with modulus-indexed length for a generated causal prefix selector.
body.consumer: Small hybrid trials can report a superpopulation ATE interval that acknowledges both the estimated ranking and the MSE choice without automatically reverting to full simultaneous width.

obligation.what_is_open: Construct and prove uniform coverage and oracle adaptation for an explicit localized multiplier interval after correcting the ranked-prefix influence function.
obligation.obstruction: The proposed multiplier resamples \(\widehat\psi_{n,k,i}\), but the proved counterexample shows that these values omit a non-negligible empirical-quantile boundary term.  The frozen assumptions also contain no uniform near-zero variance anti-concentration condition, and the handle does not specify confidence-region critical values or the localization optimization.
obligation.attempted: Considered simultaneous projection and a trial-only fallback.  Projection cannot be calibrated from the wrong covariance, while the fallback does not meet the claimed localized-diameter length or oracle-prefix equivalence requirements.
obligation.partial_result: The frozen handle cannot yet yield the advertised interval.  A necessary first repair is to use the influence function of the empirical fixed-cardinality ranked functional, including both the external empirical-quantile boundary term and the trial-generated score derivative, and to estimate its covariance.  The counterexample proved for \(\mathrm{thm:generated\text{-}prefix\text{-}coupling}\) shows that resampling the frozen values \(\widehat\psi_{n,k,i}\) targets the wrong law even at one deterministic interior prefix.  Moreover, the frozen assumptions provide no uniform anti-concentration or relative remainder condition near zero variance.  A trial-only interval avoids selection but cannot satisfy the asserted two-sided localized-diameter length characterization or oracle-prefix equivalence.  Thus the strongest proved conclusion is that coverage, localization, and oracle adaptation cannot be certified from the present handle and covariance; the interval must be redesigned after the rank-corrected coupling is established.
